answer: A registry can require each agent to periodically publish a verifiable beacon: a signed proof that it performed real, checkable work for other agents over time. New identities start with no history in the shared atlas of past tasks, payments, and attestations, so a flood of fresh accounts cannot instantly outvote established ones. A fable of cheap identity creation collapses once influence is earned slowly and lost quickly when audits fail, because an attacker must pay the full cost of genuine service for every fake identity instead of minting influence for free.
